subject: Recap + Proposed Evaluation Sprint — Mirador Tech

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + Proposed Evaluation Sprint — Mirador Tech

Hi Alex / Lina —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a concrete proposal for a short evaluation sprint so your team can validate latency, cost, and integration friction before committing to a Dedicated capacity purchase. I kept this tight so your procurement and engineering leads can skim.

Objective
- Confirm end-to-end latency under expected QPS for your search augmentation flow and validate prefix caching reduces token cost by ~30%.

Proposed success criteria (what Mirador needs to sign off on)
1) Avg token latency (inference) below 95th percentile of 220ms for 512-token requests.
2) Median token cost reduction >= 28% compared to your current endpoint (using our batching + cache config).
3) Integration: webhook + signed JWT auth working end-to-end in staging with no more than 2 minor integration issues.
4) Quality parity: sample prompt set F1 >= 0.86 vs. current baseline (we'll provide an eval harness).

Scope & deliverables (2-week sprint)
- Week 1: setup staging endpoint, ingest 5k sample prompts, baseline measurements. (Owner: Mirador eng + Redwood solutions)
- Week 2: apply batching/cache/quantization config, run load tests, shared report + walk-through. (Owner: Redwood + Mirador)
- Exit: evaluation report + recommendation for Dedicated sizing and a one-page SOW estimate.

Timeline
- Kickoff: Tue Aug 10 (30–45m)
- Baseline run: Aug 11–12
- Optimization & tests: Aug 13–16
- Final review: Aug 17 (30m)

Immediate asks / next steps
- Can you confirm engineering availability for Aug 10 kickoff (30–45m)?
- Please loop in procurement contact or let me know who from procurement should be on the thread.

I've attached a thin evaluation outline (mirador_evaluation_outline.xlsx) and an example trial config (redwood_trial_config.json) for your SRE to glance at.

If this looks good I can send a calendar invite and loop in Monica (customer success) to own onboarding and runbooks.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya.n@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Priya — this looks well scoped and reasonable. Lina and I reviewed the criteria and we can commit engineering time for the kickoff on Aug 10 at 10:00 PT.

Procurement is looped in on this thread (procurement@miradortech.com) — they will need a short SOW and an estimated cost for the two-week trial for internal approvals. Can you confirm whether Redwood requires an MSA or if a short trial agreement will suffice?

Also: two quick asks from our side
- Could you add a target for peak QPS (we anticipate 40 qps during our test window)?
- Please include a minimal runbook for handling token/credential rotation in staging.

Appreciate it. Looking forward to the kickoff.

—Alex

Hi all — happy to own onboarding and the runbook. Quick updates and attachments: evaluation-playbook.pdf (walkthrough + checklist) and a shared Drive folder with scripts.

Answers to procurement question
- For a 2-week evaluation we typically use a short trial addendum (no MSA required). I'll attach the addendum and a one-page SOW estimate.
- Trial credit model: we propose a capped credit of $1,200 equivalent (covers expected test volume at 40 QPS). If you want raw numbers I included an estimated cost table in the SOW.

Operational notes / what we need from Mirador before kickoff
1) A staging service account email + list of IPs (if you require IP allowlisting).
2) A small sample of 3k–5k prompts and a representative token-length distribution file (we have a template in the Drive folder).
3) Point person for on-call during test window (name + mobile).
